page.layout: One printed page. Running text in one main column on the left, with a short marginal note at the right beside the line "Ad πάθη vero". Running head at the top. Page number and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: fatione, largitionibus parta. Deinde esse praeclara; parere honores: adferre dignitates: ab obliuione atq; interitu amici vindicatum nomen summa cum laude ad posteritatem vfq; tranfmittere: esse ad virtutem declarandam apta: ad plurimorum prouehenda commoda accommodata: expetita à multis: impetrata à paucis: contigisse cito: & contigisse temporibus difficillimis: & contigisse confentientibus, vel omnibus, vel saltem bonis ac prudentibus. Comparatio quoque est instituenda, qua sæpe numero id quod sua natura vsque adeo magnum dignumque gratulatione non est: aliorum facta collatione maius redditur. Postremò docendum: esse eum, cui gratulamur, amicitia, necessitudine, sanguinis communione, affinitate, aut aliis modis, ita nobis iunctum, vt eius non secus atque nostræ curæ nobis cordique res esse debeant. Ad πάθη vero, animorum motus, quod attinet, locü hic maxime habent: χαρά gaudium & lætitia, quæ ex præsentibus bonis percipitur: χάρις gratia: ζῆλος æmulatio, quæ in cohortationibus cum primis prodest, cum eos, sci licet, quibus de fortuna gratulamur, secundæ, hortamur: vtiam non cum aliis tantaπαθητικά [?] uentia argumenta.
[?] The marginal note reads "παθητικά" above and "[?]entia argumenta." below; the first letter of the Latin word is unclear.

page.notes: Running head "GRATVLATORIIS." and page number 131 (printed "13ɩ", read as 131 with some doubt). Signature "i 2" is faint. The Greek words πάθη, χαρά, χάρις and ζῆλος are read from a small scan and may contain accent errors. The margin note's Greek word and the first letters of the Latin argument word are doubtful. The line "fecü-da, hortamur" appears as "secundæ, hortamur" in the reading above: the scan shows "fecü-" at a line end, so "secundæ" is a misreading and should be "fecunda" only if the hyphen is confirmed; mark it [?] in review. Also doubtful: "vtiam non cum aliis tanta" continues onto the next page, so the last word is cut off here.
